conviction_note: FY26 is pre-released (ahead of the £37.2m bar; company-compiled consensus since moved to £38.4m), so the move lives in the first quantified guide on the national-network build (20+ new warehouses, up to 700 drivers, £375m a year of new contract revenue from 2027-2030). That guide is a scheduled guidance event on a thin, 3-analyst, $0.5m/day name, so abs_move is set at 7.5. Its sign is not knowable from public documents: the stock has re-rated about 30% since June on the revenue, the largest holder (Aberforth) has sold into that rally, and the costs are unquantified. So p_up is 47, and the scaled number is -0.45 against an impact_sum of -1.4. The gap is the uncertainty about the sign, not a disagreement between the two measurements.

findings.finding: The release carries the first quantified guidance on the cost of going national, a build the domestic trade press puts at more than 20 new warehouses and up to 700 subcontract drivers, against a ~£203m market cap and ~£38m of operating profit. The FY27 guide will therefore carry a large one-off and transition-cost number that the company has so far refused to quantify.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior quantified guidance on this programme. The contract-win RNS moved the stock +9.8% (17 Jun), +3.9% (29 Jun), +4.5% (17 Jul) and +5.6% (15 Oct), so the revenue side has been rewarded each time. The last two finals moved +8.42% (Nov 2024, with a special dividend) and +4.11% (Nov 2025).
findings.original_quote: Smiths News expects to open more than 20 new warehouses ... plans to recruit up to 700 subcontract drivers (paraphrased by WebFetch from Better Retailing; the company's own RNS says only 'one-off implementation costs during FY2027 as well as early-life transition costs')
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has re-rated from ~63p to 82p (+30%) on four revenue announcements while the cost side is still unquantified. Edison's DCF of 96p is explicitly 'unchanged pending further guidance', and consensus exists only for FY26. If the market had priced a costly build, the share would not have kept rising on each contract RNS. Against that: management has committed to fund it from existing resources and hold the dividend at or above 5.2p, which bounds a financing or dividend shock. The sign is therefore an inference, and the finding is kept small with a wide range.
findings.independence: Company RNS of 17 Jun 2026 confirms one-off FY27 implementation costs and transition costs exist: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/smiths-news--snws/contract-win-national-distribution/9621741 . Edison notes the costs are unquantified: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/100-uk-transformational-contract-win/BM-3544/

findings.finding: FY26 adjusted operating profit will be ahead of the £37.2m the company cited and probably a little ahead of the £38.4m consensus it has since compiled, but the beat was pre-released on 29 September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 29 Sep 2026 'ahead' trading update moved +4.44% and the price followed through to 78.6p by 2 Oct. FY24 and FY25 finals that beat moved +8.42% and +4.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: It mostly is: the consensus page already shows £38.4m after the update, and the stock re-rated on the TU. All that is left is the gap between 'ahead' and the revised consensus.

findings.finding: FY26 contained a record World Cup contribution of over £3m (~8% of operating profit) that the company says recurs only in alternate years, so the FY27 profit guide faces that lap before any transition cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None separable. FY25 (Euros year) final moved +4.11%. The FY24 lap was not observable.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company flagged the alternate-year pattern itself and the three brokers will model it. What may not be priced is a headline FY27 profit guide below FY26 once the lap and transition costs are combined, which a retail-heavy register (the company runs a separate retail webcast) may read on the headline. Kept small.
findings.independence: Edison's June FY27e (EPS 10.49p vs 10.76p FY26e) already builds in a decline: https://www.edisongroup.com/research/100-uk-transformational-contract-win/BM-3544/

findings.finding: The largest shareholder, Aberforth Partners, has sold steadily into the contract-driven rally, from 17.21% (3 Aug) to 15.913% to 14.828% on 28 Oct (about 2.7m shares in October, on a day the tape shows 1.33m traded). That is a known, active seller who can supply stock into any positive reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock still rose from 75.6p to 83.8p during the October selling, so the seller has been absorbed so far.
findings.why_not_priced: TR-1s are public, but on a $0.5m/day name a holder of 36.7m shares (~70 days of turnover) still selling is a supply overhang that caps upside more than the price shows. If it were priced, the stock would not be sitting at its high going into the print.

outside_window.finding: The contracts go live July 2027 (News UK), October 2027 (TMG), January 2028 (ANL) and April 2030 (Frontline/Seymour); earnings accretion is guided from FY28. Execution risk and benefit are both realised years after this window.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative, which agrees in sign with priced_lean_pct (-0.43, driven by the +11% 20-day run-up). They cut against the name's history of positive finals (+8.4%, +4.1%) and its rally on every contract RNS. p_up is therefore held near 50 rather than following the findings.
language_note: The domestic trade press (Better Retailing, 18 Jul 2026) carried the physical scale of the build: more than 20 new warehouses, up to 700 subcontract drivers, and Scotland as new territory. The RNS and the wire copy (HL/Sharecast, AJ Bell) carried only 'one-off implementation costs' with no scale.

The company's own site (14 Oct 2026, not an RNS) carried the appointment of a Transformation Director and a dedicated implementation team. That is consistent with a large programme, but it carries no numbers.
